import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1041

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1041](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1041)
-/

open Polynomial MeasureTheory ENNReal

namespace Erdos1041

variable (n : ℕ) (f : ℂ[X]) (hn : n ≥ 2) (hnum : f.natDegree = n)
variable (h_monic : f.Monic)
variable (h : f.rootSet ℂ ⊆ Metric.ball 0 1)
include hn hnum h h_monic

/--
The length of a subset $s$ of $\mathbb{C}$ is defined to be its 1-dimensional
Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(s)$.
-/
noncomputable def length (s : Set ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ := μH[1] s

open scoped Classical in
/--
**Erdős–Herzog–Piranian Component Lemma** (Metric Properties of Polynomials, 1958):
If $f$ is a monic degree $n$ polynomial with all roots in the unit disk,
then some connected component
of $\{z \mid |f(z)| < 1\}$ contains at least two roots with multiplicity.

See p. 139, above Problem 5:
[EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., _Metric properties of polynomials_.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 32]
theorem exists_connected_component_contains_two_roots :
    ∃ C, C ⊆ {z | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1} ∧ IsConnected C ∧
      2 ≤ (f.roots.filter (· ∈ C)).card := by
  sorry

/--
Let
$$ f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} (z - z_i) \in \mathbb{C}[x] $$
with $|z_i| < 1$ for all $i$.

Conjecture: Must there always exist a path of length less than 2 in
$$ \{ z \in \mathbb{C} \mid |f(z)| < 1 \} $$
which connects two of the roots of $f$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 32]
theorem erdos_1041 :
    ∃ (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) (h : ({z₁, z₂} : Multiset ℂ) ≤ f.roots) (γ : Path z₁ z₂),
      Set.range γ ⊆ { z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1 } ∧ length (Set.range γ) < 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos1041

reformulations.difference: The source asserts the existence of a connected component containing two root occurrences; Lean only requires a connected subset C of the sublevel set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any connected C ⊆ U, choose x ∈ C. Then C ⊆ connectedComponentIn U x. Enlarging C cannot decrease the cardinality of the filtered root multiset, so the component also contains at least two root occurrences. Conversely, a connected component is itself a connected subset. The exact equivalence with the formulation using connectedComponentIn was proved as Review1041.component_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean bounds the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the path's image, using Erdos1041.length, rather than the ordinary length of the parametrized path.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These lengths need not agree for an individual path that retraces itself, but the existential statements are equivalent. A rectifiable path has image Hausdorff measure at most its ordinary length. Conversely, if a continuous path between distinct endpoints has image Hausdorff measure less than 2, its image contains a simple arc joining those endpoints. That arc has Hausdorff measure at most that of the original image; a simple arc's ordinary length equals its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, so it is rectifiable and has length less than 2. It remains inside the same sublevel set. For equal endpoints, the multiset constraint requires a root of multiplicity at least two, and a constant path works under either length convention. Thus ignoring retracing does not change this existential conjecture.
